data_gaps.reason: no crime baseline: no NCVS or other official U.S. table records ethnic Jewish offenders against non-Hispanic White victims; story counts only, no CDI.

not coded yet. AP and NYT sample URLs returned errors or bot protection from our build machine; WaPo pages could not be retrieved (timeout/404), which is a fetch failure, not a demonstrated paywall. CDI is null for these outlets.
the NCVS does not cover homicide; the baseline is nonfatal violent incidents (rape/sexual assault, robbery, aggravated and simple assault).

the story frame was built from keyword queries, most of them anti-Black framings ("white supremacist", "anti-Black", "racially motivated", "hate crime"); only "anti-white" and "Black supremacist" target the reverse framing. Black-on-White crime stories that use none of these phrases are not in the frame, so the pilot frame is expected to under-sample them. This is a pre-registered alternative explanation (label convention, query misfire).
single coder (joseph-a) so far; the method requires a second coder and an agreement rate before results are reported.
BJS published only percentages (Table 14) for 2018, not counts; count is null and not derived.

sample_weight, sample_order and fetch_status (coded file only) are not in the agreed v1.1 columns and were dropped; they remain in Joseph's pilot folder. Sample weights are constant within an outlet, so they do not change a within-outlet W_on_B : B_on_W ratio.
Rows outside the 300-row random sample are uncoded frame rows (coded=false, coding fields blank).
Uncoded sample rows keep blank coding fields; nothing was inferred.

judgement_calls: stories_W_on_B / stories_B_on_W count coded stories with include=true in that direction, from any query phrase. pilot_method.md names the "anti-Black" / "anti-white" phrase pair as the primary CDI pair; format v1.1 does not restrict by phrase. Under the phrase-pair rule the 2023 pilot would have 0 included stories in both cells. To be settled with Joseph.
When both media cells are 0, cdi is null (a +0.5/+0.5 adjustment would produce a number with no stories behind it).

Rates (headline_rate, pct_first_para, photo_rate) and stance counts use included stories (include=true, any direction, including 'other'); each rate's denominator is given in the matching *_n field. pct_first_para = share whose first racial mention is in the headline (para 1) or first body paragraph (para 2).
stories_total = all rows for the outlet in stories_<year>.csv, i.e. keyword-matched Media Cloud hits (volume only), not coded crime stories.

CDI uses the raw NCVS incident ratio for the same year (not population-adjusted), as pre-registered. NCVS counts are survey estimates with standard errors (ncvs_*_se); the CDI carries that uncertainty and the much larger uncertainty of small story counts.
Sample weights are not applied: they are constant within an outlet, so the within-outlet ratio is the same weighted or unweighted.
